title: Senegalese Black-Eyed Pea Salad (Saladou Niébé)
subtitle: Recipe Formulation Sheet
blurb: Cooked black-eyed peas cut with uniformly diced peppers and onion, dressed in lime and olive oil, then cured cold for 30 minutes.
scalingPrinciple: Lock Item A.01 at 100.0% to serve as the mathematical baseline weight. All subsequent component percentages are calculated relative to that baseline. Volumetric values map to the current baseline target scale and must be dynamically scaled via weight calculations for larger yields.

rows.name: Cooked Black-Eyed Peas
rows.role: Primary foundational ingredient; locks baseline mass.

rows.name: Red Onion
rows.role: Sharp aromatic profile, savory crunch, and color contrast.

rows.name: Red Bell Pepper
rows.role: Crisp sweet element, structural body, and visual inclusion.

rows.name: Green Bell Pepper
rows.role: Crisp vegetal element, balanced bitterness, and color contrast.

rows.name: Fresh Lime Juice
rows.role: Acid profile; denatures raw onions and brightens overall profile.

rows.name: Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
rows.role: Lipid vehicle; rich mouthfeel coat and suspension base for dressing.

rows.name: Kosher Salt
rows.role: Primary electrolyte seasoning; flavor enhancer and cell wall softener.

rows.name: Black Pepper
rows.role: Secondary warming spice profile; subtle pungent top note.

rows.name: Fresh Flat-Leaf Parsley
rows.role: Finishing herb bed; provides clean, earthy chlorophyll notes.

rows.name: Bird's Eye Chili (Optional)
rows.role: Optional heat modifier; introduces localized capsicum spikes.

mise.label: Substrate Hydration & Cooling (A.01)
mise.text: Ensure cooked black-eyed peas are completely cooled to room temperature, thoroughly rinsed under cold water, and entirely drained of excess unbound moisture to prevent starch bleeding.

mise.label: Uniform Vegetable Dicing (B.01–B.03)
mise.text: Core, seed, and finely dice the red and green bell peppers to a uniform 1/4" specification to precisely match the physical geometry of the black-eyed peas. Finely dice the red onion to a matching profile.

mise.label: Herb Comminution (C.01)
mise.text: Wash, spin dry completely, and finely chop flat-leaf parsley, isolating leaf tissue and discarding thick structural stems.

mise.label: Citrus Extraction (B.04)
mise.text: Express fresh lime juice mechanically, filtering out internal pulp and seeds to maintain a completely clear liquid state.

execution.name: Base Amalgamation
execution.text: In a clean, non-reactive stainless steel mixing vessel, combine the cooled black-eyed peas (A.01), diced red onion (B.01), red bell pepper (B.02), green bell pepper (B.03), and chopped parsley (C.01). If using the optional bird's eye chili (C.02), incorporate it at this step. Toss gently with a silicone spatula to achieve homogenous distribution without marring the exterior skins of the legumes.

execution.name: Dressing Emulsification
execution.text: In a separate glass or stainless bowl, combine the fresh lime juice (B.04), kosher salt (B.06), and black pepper (B.07). Whisk vigorously until the salt crystals are entirely dissolved in the acid phase. While continuing to whisk, slowly stream in the extra-virgin olive oil (B.05) to create a temporary uniform suspension.

execution.name: Matrix Integration & Curing Wait-State
execution.text: Pour the whisked dressing immediately over the base amalgamation. Fold the salad delicately using an under-and-over sweeping motion to fully coat all component surfaces without crushing the ingredients. Seal the vessel with an airtight lid and transfer to cold storage for a minimum 30-minute marination wait state to permit osmotic flavor equilibration. Give it a brief toss right before serving.

qc.target: Legumes must retain an al dente, resilient core profile with zero mushy collapse; raw vegetables must deliver a clean, crisp mechanical snap.
Uniform color distribution showing high contrast between deep red, vibrant green, and pale cream; all surfaces coated in a thin, translucent gloss sheen with zero pooled liquid at the base.

directive: Execute all blending motions manually with low shear forces to preserve physical structural definition. Ensure the substrate is below 45°F before dressing application to prevent thermal wilting of the aromatic herbs.
